mainTopic: חצר קטנה שנפרצה לגדולה — the one-way rule of breached courtyards, and אביי's objection that a מחיצה here causes an איסור
overview: This amud finishes a ברייתא about a small courtyard whose shared wall with a large courtyard has broken open. The gap counts as a doorway of the large courtyard, so the large courtyard spreads into the small one, but the small one does not spread into the large one. The ברייתא applies this one-way rule to כלאים, a גט, a שליח ציבור, a מנין, and reciting קריאת שמע near צואה. אביי objects that, in the כלאים case, the wall makes things stricter than an open field, where one would only need to keep four אמות from the vines. He calls this a 'מחיצה לאיסור', a partition that forbids. רבי זירא challenges him from a משנה: evening out the edges of a breached large courtyard would make it forbidden. אביי answers that building those walls really counts as removing partitions. רבא then raises a new challenge, and the teaching he quotes comes on the next amud.

steps.title: Vines and seeds across the broken wall
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא finishes the כלאים case: if vines are in the large courtyard and someone sowed seeds in the small one, the seeds are forbidden but the vines stay permitted. If vines are in the small courtyard, one may even sow seeds in the large one from the start.
steps.simpleTranslation: The vines are permitted. If there are vines in the small courtyard, it is permitted to sow the large one.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא is finishing a case it started on the previous amud: vines in the large courtyard, where someone sowed seeds in the small one. The seeds are forbidden, but this line says the vines stay permitted. Then it adds that if the vines are in the small courtyard, you may sow seeds in the large courtyard from the start.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The small courtyard counts as part of the large one. So when vines are in the large courtyard, the whole small courtyard is treated as their vineyard area, and seeds sown there become forbidden. The vines themselves stay permitted, because they are not treated as being inside the small courtyard. For the same reason, vines in the small courtyard do not count as being in the large one, so sowing in the large courtyard is allowed from the start.

keyTerms.meaning: The forbidden mixing of seeds with grapevines

steps.confusionAlert: This amud opens in the middle of a sentence. 'גפנים מותרין' is the end of the case before it: vines in the large courtyard, and seeds sown in the small one. In that case the seeds are forbidden but the vines are permitted.

phrases.english: The vines are permitted.
phrases.notes: End of the earlier case: vines in the large courtyard, seeds sown in the small one. The seeds are forbidden, but the vines are not.

phrases.english: If there are vines in the small courtyard —
it is permitted to sow the large one.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the כלאים clause of the ברייתא that began on the previous amud.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The small courtyard is drawn into the large one, but the large one is not drawn into the small. Vines in the large courtyard forbid seeds sown in the small one, but the vines themselves stay permitted. Vines in the small courtyard do not prevent sowing in the large one.

steps.title: Divorce across the broken wall
steps.stepSummary: If the wife stands in the large courtyard and the גט lands in the small one, she is divorced. If she stands in the small courtyard and the גט lands in the large one, she is not divorced.
steps.simpleTranslation: If the wife is in the large courtyard and the גט is in the small one, she is divorced. If the wife is in the small courtyard and the גט is in the large one, she is not divorced.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא applies the same one-way rule to גיטין: where the wife stands compared to where the גט lands.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A גט thrown into a woman's courtyard works when she is considered to be right there. If she is in the large courtyard, the small courtyard counts as part of where she is, so a גט landing there reaches her. If she is in the small courtyard, the large courtyard does not count as part of her place, so the גט does not reach her.

phrases.english: If the wife is in the large courtyard and the bill of divorce is in the small one — she is divorced.
phrases.notes: The small courtyard counts as part of her large one.

phrases.aramaic: אִשָּׁה בַּקְּטַנָּה וְגֵט בַּגְּדוֹלָה — אֵינָהּ מִתְגָּרֶשֶׁת.
phrases.english: If the wife is in the small courtyard and the bill of divorce is in the large one — she is not divorced.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new application of the same one-way rule, now in divorce law.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A woman in the large courtyard is divorced by a גט landing in the small one, but not the reverse.

steps.title: Congregation and prayer leader across the broken wall
steps.stepSummary: If the congregation is in the large courtyard and the שליח ציבור is in the small one, they fulfill their obligation through him. If the positions are reversed, they do not.
steps.simpleTranslation: If the congregation is in the large courtyard and the prayer leader is in the small one, they fulfill their obligation. If the congregation is in the small courtyard and the prayer leader is in the large one, they do not fulfill their obligation.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא applies the rule to prayer: whether the שליח ציבור can make the congregation יוצא when they are in different courtyards.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The congregation must be considered together in one place with the שליח ציבור. When the congregation is in the large courtyard, the small courtyard where the leader stands counts as part of their area, so they are together. When the congregation is in the small courtyard, the leader's large courtyard does not count as part of theirs, so they are apart.

keyTerms.meaning: The prayer leader who prays on behalf of the congregation

phrases.english: If the congregation is in the large courtyard and the prayer leader is in the small one —
they fulfill their obligation.
If the congregation is in the small courtyard and the prayer leader is in the large one —
they do not fulfill their obligation.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A third application of the same one-way rule, now in communal prayer.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A congregation in the large courtyard is יוצא through a שליח ציבור in the small courtyard, but not the reverse.

steps.title: Counting a מנין across the broken wall
steps.stepSummary: Nine men in the large courtyard and one in the small one join to make a מנין. Nine in the small courtyard and one in the large one do not join.
steps.simpleTranslation: If nine are in the large courtyard and one is in the small one, they join together. If nine are in the small courtyard and one is in the large one, they do not join together.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא gives its last application: whether ten men split between the two courtyards can join to form a מנין.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The single man in the small courtyard counts as standing in the large courtyard, so he joins the nine there. When the nine are in the small courtyard, the man in the large courtyard is not counted as being with them, so there is no מנין. Notice the direction depends only on which courtyard is which, not on where most of the people are.

keyTerms.meaning: They join together (to complete the count)

steps.whatToRemember: One rule runs through all these cases. A small courtyard broken open into a large one is treated as part of the large one, like a doorway of it. So whatever is in the large courtyard 'reaches' into the small one: the wife, the congregation, the nine men. Whatever is only in the small courtyard does not reach into the large one.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the majority decides. In the second case nine people are in the small courtyard and they still cannot join the one man. What decides is the size of the courtyards, not the number of people.

phrases.english: If nine are in the large courtyard and one individual is in the small one — they join together.

phrases.aramaic: תִּשְׁעָה בַּקְּטַנָּה וְאֶחָד בַּגְּדוֹלָה — אֵין מִצְטָרְפִין.
phrases.english: If nine are in the small courtyard and one is in the large one — they do not join together.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: The final application in the ברייתא's list, now for counting a מנין.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An individual in the small courtyard joins nine in the large one to make a מנין, but nine in the small courtyard do not join with one in the large one.
steps.whyThisMatters: These four cases show that the rule about breached courtyards is a general rule about place. The same rule shapes הלכות far beyond carrying on שבת: כלאים, גיטין, תפילה, and מנין.

steps.title: Excrement and reciting שמע across the two courtyards
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא's final case: צואה in the large courtyard forbids קריאת שמע in the small one. צואה in the small courtyard does not forbid קריאת שמע in the large one.
steps.simpleTranslation: If there is excrement in the large courtyard, it is forbidden to recite שמע in the small one. If there is excrement in the small courtyard, it is permitted to recite שמע in the large one.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא gives one more example of its pattern, this time about קריאת שמע near צואה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The small courtyard is treated as part of the large one, so צואה in the large courtyard counts as being in the small one too. But the large courtyard has its own walls on the sides, so it is a separate space from the small one. That is why צואה in the small courtyard does not affect it.

keyTerms.meaning: Excrement. One may not say holy words in its presence.
The large courtyard and the small courtyard

steps.whatToRemember: In every case in this ברייתא, the large courtyard 'swallows' the small one, but the small one never swallows the large one.

phrases.english: Excrement in the large courtyard:
it is forbidden to recite Shema in the small one.
Excrement in the small courtyard:
it is permitted to recite Shema in the large one.

steps.triggerLanguage: צוֹאָה בַּגְּדוֹלָה אָסוּר לִקְרוֹת קְרִיאַת שְׁמַע בַּקְּטַנָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The last item in the same list of cases from the ברייתא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: צואה in the large courtyard forbids קריאת שמע in the small one, but not the reverse.

steps.title: אביי objects that the partition here creates a prohibition
steps.stepSummary: אביי argues that the ברייתא's כלאים ruling leads to a strange result. The partition causes an איסור, because without any partition one could simply keep four אמות away from the vines and sow.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to them: If so, we have found a partition that causes a prohibition! For if there were no partition at all, one would keep four cubits away from the vines and sow. Yet now, with the partition, the whole small courtyard is forbidden!
steps.whatsHappening: אביי challenges the ברייתא's כלאים ruling. He says it makes a wall work backwards, causing an איסור instead of helping.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Usually a מחיצה separates spaces and makes things more permitted. According to the ברייתא, vines in the large courtyard forbid sowing anywhere in the small one. In an open field, you would only need to keep four אמות away. So the walls are making things stricter, which seems illogical to אביי.

keyTerms.meaning: A partition that causes a prohibition, the opposite of its usual effect
Four cubits, the distance one must keep between vines and seeds

steps.confusionAlert: אביי is not saying the vines aren't vines, or that כלאים doesn't apply. He is only objecting that the walls make the result stricter than having no walls at all.

phrases.english: Abaye said to them:
If so, we have found a partition that causes a prohibition.
For if there were no partition,
one would keep four cubits away and sow,
whereas now it is forbidden!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the כלאים ruling from the start of the ברייתא (Step 1).
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's ruling that vines in the large courtyard forbid sowing anywhere in the small one.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A partition should never make things stricter than having no partition at all. Here it does, which seems unreasonable.

steps.title: רבי זירא cites the משנה about a breached courtyard
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא pushes back on אביי by quoting a משנה. When a large courtyard is breached into a small one, the large one may carry but the small one may not, because the breach counts as the large courtyard's doorway.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי זירא said to אביי: Haven't we found a partition that causes a prohibition? But we learned in a משנה: A large courtyard that was breached into a small one: the large one is permitted and the small one is forbidden, because the breach is like the doorway of the large one.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי זירא begins his answer to אביי by quoting a משנה. This sets up the point he will draw from it in the next line.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה is about carrying on שבת. The large courtyard keeps its wall-edges on both sides of the gap, so the gap looks like a doorway in its wall, and it may still carry. The small courtyard has lost its whole wall on that side, so it may not carry.

keyTerms.meaning: But we learned in a משנה. This introduces a source used as a challenge or proof.
Was breached, meaning its wall was broken open

phrases.english: Rabbi Zeira said to Abaye:
And haven't we found a partition that causes a prohibition?!
But we learned in a Mishnah:
A large courtyard that was breached into a small one:
the large one is permitted and the small one is forbidden,
because the breach is like the doorway of the large one.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְלֹא מָצִינוּ מְחִיצָה לְאִיסּוּר וְהָא תְּנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Responds to אביי's objection by bringing a source.
steps.raayaObject: That a מחיצה can sometimes cause an איסור.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה about a large courtyard breached into a small one.

steps.title: Evening out the walls would forbid the large courtyard
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא draws his point from the משנה. If someone built walls to remove the large courtyard's protruding edges, the large courtyard would become forbidden too. So partitions can cause an איסור.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if he were to even out its protruding edges, the large courtyard would also be forbidden!
steps.whatsHappening: רבי זירא finishes his challenge by drawing the point from the משנה: here, adding walls would create an איסור.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The large courtyard is permitted only because its wall sticks out past the small courtyard on each side. If someone added walls inside the large courtyard to line it up with the small one's width, the gap would no longer look like a doorway, and the large courtyard would become fully breached and forbidden. Adding a מחיצה there causes an איסור, so a 'partition that prohibits' is nothing new.

keyTerms.meaning: Its protruding wall-edges, the parts of the large courtyard's wall that stick out beyond the small one

steps.whatToRemember: רבי זירא argues that adding walls can sometimes forbid, using the breached-courtyard case. Watch for אביי's reply in the next step, which rejects this proof.
steps.whyThisMatters: This defends the ברייתא's whole pattern from Steps 1–5 against אביי's logical objection.

phrases.english: And if he were to even out its protruding edges,
the large one would also be forbidden!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִילּוּ הִשְׁוָה אֶת גִּיפּוּפֶיהָ גְּדוֹלָה נָמֵי אֲסוּרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the conclusion from the משנה quoted in Step 7.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects אביי's assumption that a partition can never cause an איסור.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: אביי assumed partitions only permit. The משנה shows that building walls to even out the large courtyard's protrusions would forbid it.
steps.kashyaTarget: אביי's claim (Step 6) that we never find a מחיצה that causes an איסור.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: In the breached-courtyard משנה, building walls to even out the large courtyard's protrusions would make it forbidden. So a partition can cause an איסור.

steps.title: אביי: Those Walls Actually Remove Partitions
steps.stepSummary: אביי answers רבי זירא. In the breached-courtyard case, building walls to even out the edges counts as removing partitions, not adding them.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to him (to רבי זירא): There, it is a removal of partitions.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי pushes back on רבי זירא's proof. He says the courtyard case does not show a partition causing an איסור.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the courtyard case, the large courtyard's protruding edges are what let the breach count as its doorway, so it may carry. Building walls to even out those edges erases that setup. Legally, these walls cancel the original partitions. So the איסור comes from taking partitions away, and אביי's point stands: adding a real partition should not create an איסור.

keyTerms.meaning: He said to him (introduces a reply to the last speaker)

steps.confusionAlert: In the courtyard case, someone physically builds new walls, but אביי says this counts as removing partitions. Halachically, what matters is the effect: these walls erase the protruding edges that gave the large courtyard its status.

phrases.english: He (Abaye) said to him (Rabbi Zeira):
phrases.notes: אביי is answering רבי זירא's proof from Step 8.

phrases.english: There, it is a removal of partitions.
phrases.notes: The added walls cancel the courtyard's original partition setup.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ, הָתָם סִילּוּק מְחִיצּוֹת הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects רבי זירא's proof (Step 8) that partitions can cause an איסור.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the proof from the breached-courtyard משנה as a case of a partition causing an איסור.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The walls in that case do not add partitions. They remove the original ones, so the איסור comes from removal, not from a new partition.

steps.title: רבא Asks: Have We Never Found a Partition That Forbids?
steps.stepSummary: רבא challenges אביי's claim that a partition cannot cause an איסור, and begins to quote a teaching to prove otherwise.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said to אביי: And have we not found a partition that causes an איסור? But it was stated:
steps.whatsHappening: רבא opens a new challenge to אביי. This line only sets it up; the actual teaching רבא quotes comes right on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי's whole position is that it is strange for a מחיצה to cause an איסור. רבא disagrees and claims there is a known case where it does. The words 'וְהָא אִתְּמַר' signal that an earlier teaching of the אמוראים is about to be brought as the source.

keyTerms.meaning: A partition that causes an איסור
But was it not stated? (introduces a teaching of the אמוראים as proof)

phrases.english: Rava said to Abaye:
And have we not found a partition that causes prohibition?
phrases.notes: A rhetorical question that works as a challenge.

phrases.english: But was it not stated:
phrases.notes: Setup. The quoted teaching comes on the next amud.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רָבָא לְאַבָּיֵי: וְלֹא מָצִינוּ מְחִיצָה לְאִיסּוּר? וְהָא אִתְּמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After אביי deflects רבי זירא, רבא raises a fresh challenge against the same position.
steps.kashyaTarget: אביי's assumption (Steps 6 and 9) that a partition should not cause an איסור.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If a known teaching of the אמוראים shows a partition causing an איסור, then אביי's objection to the ברייתא's כלאים ruling falls away.
